analysis: The PR changes only docs/provider/cli-reference.md: the 'Last updated' date (line 3) and a parenthetical at line 52 saying inline video (data:video/mp4 or quicktime) may be constant or variable frame rate. Both changed ranges lie outside the supplied head excerpts (lines 822-1671), so I reviewed the surrounding documentation, not the changed lines. The change is documentation-only. It alters no code, trust boundary, authorization, attestation, encryption, key custody or billing control. It claims no new security guarantee. Relevant threats are T-050 (inline video plaintext in provider temp files), T-056 and TB-007. The VFR note describes media decoding scope. I cannot verify that VFR decoding is implemented safely, or that it still avoids plaintext temp files (T-050), because no code was supplied. A VFR decode path would be new parsing surface for adversarial consumer video input, so any code change behind this doc should be reviewed against T-050 and bounds and DoS limits. This PR contains no such code. The visible docs (stop/restart drain, logout, App Attest, fan, report, cache key descriptions) are unchanged context and do not contradict the threat model, and no pre-existing issue is restated. The T-041 cache details (30-minute TTL, DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE) are not altered. No findings; the integration pass should check whether the actual VFR video decoder change lives in other PR files.
